linked_stories.title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial in Mark

people.name: Caiaphas
people.summary: The high priest in the year of Jesus' death. After Lazarus is raised, John records him saying it is better for one man to die for the people. John interprets those words through Caiaphas's role as high priest. Matthew describes leaders plotting Jesus' arrest in his palace. After Jesus is brought there, Caiaphas tears his clothes at Jesus' reply. John calls Annas his father-in-law. Luke names Annas and Caiaphas together as high priests. Acts includes Caiaphas among the rulers questioning Peter and John.

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.summary: A wealthy chief tax collector in Jericho. Luke says he is short and climbs a sycomore tree to see Jesus. Jesus calls him by name and says he must stay at his house. The crowd objects that Jesus is visiting a sinner. Zacchaeus says he gives half his goods to the poor and repays any false charges fourfold. Luke records Jesus saying salvation has come to the house. Jesus describes his mission as seeking and saving the lost.

people.name: Thomas
people.summary: One of the Twelve, called Didymus, meaning twin. In John, he urges the others to go with Jesus after Lazarus dies: “Let us also go, that we may die with him”. At supper, he asks about the way; Jesus replies, “I am the way, the truth, and the life”. He misses Jesus' first appearance to the gathered disciples after the resurrection. He says he will not believe without seeing the nail marks and touching Jesus' side. John describes another appearance eight days later, when Thomas answers, “My Lord and my God”. He is later present at the sea of Tiberias and named in the upper-room gathering.

geography.origin: Not stated; one of the Twelve (Matthew 10:3)

linked_stories.title: Breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias

people.name: Stephen
people.summary: One of seven chosen in Acts to help distribute food to widows among Greek-speaking disciples. The language description does not assign a modern nationality. Acts describes him as full of faith, the Holy Spirit and power, and doing wonders. Men from several synagogues dispute with him and accuse him of speaking against the temple and law. His defence retells Israel's history and accuses his hearers of resisting the Holy Spirit. Acts describes him seeing Jesus at God's right hand. He is stoned outside the city while praying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit”, and asking forgiveness for his attackers. Saul approves his death.

people.name: Barnabas
people.summary: Joses, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles call Barnabas. Acts 4:36 explains the name as “The son of consolation”, or encouragement. He sells land and gives the money to the apostles. He introduces Saul to the apostles and supports his account of preaching in Damascus. Sent to Antioch, he welcomes what Acts calls God's grace. Acts praises his character, faith and fullness of the Holy Spirit. He brings Saul from Tarsus, and Antioch's church sends them on a journey. Later, he wants John Mark to join them. A sharp dispute with Paul separates them; Barnabas sails to Cyprus with Mark.

people.name: Philip the evangelist
people.summary: One of the seven chosen with Stephen at Jerusalem. After the persecution following Stephen's death, Acts describes Philip preaching Christ in Samaria, where men and women are baptized. An angel directs him toward Gaza. He meets an Ethiopian officer reading Isaiah, explains the passage and baptizes him. Acts then describes Philip being carried away and found at Azotus. He preaches along the coast to Caesarea. Years later, Paul's group stays at his home there, where he has four unmarried daughters who prophesy. This profile is separate from Philip the apostle.

people.name: Cornelius
people.summary: A Roman officer in the Italian unit at Caesarea. Acts describes him and his household as devoted to God, with Cornelius giving to the poor and praying often. It describes an angel telling him to send for Peter at Joppa while Peter has a vision. Cornelius gathers relatives and close friends. Acts says the Holy Spirit comes upon those listening to Peter. Peter directs their baptism and stays at their request. Later, Peter explains the visit in Jerusalem. In Acts 11:18, his listeners conclude that God has granted life-giving repentance to non-Jews.

people.name: Silas
people.summary: A leader in Jerusalem's church, sent with Judas Barsabas to bring its council's letter to Antioch. Acts describes him as a prophet who encourages the believers. After Paul's dispute with Barnabas, Paul chooses Silas as a companion. At Philippi, they are beaten and jailed. Acts describes them praying and singing at midnight before an earthquake. Silas stays with Timothy at Berea and later rejoins Paul at Corinth. Letters name Silvanus with Paul and Timothy and mention his preaching among the Corinthians. The proposed Silas/Silvanus link remains qualified; the name forms alone do not prove it.

people.name: Timothy
people.summary: A disciple whom Acts introduces at Lystra, without stating his birthplace. His mother is a Jewish believer and his father is Greek. Local believers speak well of him. Paul takes him along and circumcises him because of the Jews in that region. He stays with Silas at Berea, rejoins Paul at Corinth and travels into Asia. Paul's letters call him his son in faith and recall the faith of Lois, his grandmother, and Eunice, his mother. First Timothy 1:3 places him at Ephesus. His father's name is not supplied here.

geography.origin: Birthplace not stated; Acts 16:1 introduces him at Lystra.

people.name: Apollos
people.summary: A Jew born in Alexandria, described in Acts as a skilled speaker with strong knowledge of scripture. He teaches in Ephesus while knowing only John's baptism. Aquila and Priscilla explain God's way to him more fully. With letters from the believers, he goes to Achaia and helps those who believe. In First Corinthians, Paul writes, “I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase”. A later letter asks that Apollos and Zenas receive help for their journey. No claim about authorship of Hebrews is made here.

people.name: Priscilla
people.summary: Aquila's wife, who leaves Italy with him after Claudius orders Jews to leave Rome. Acts 18:2 names Aquila as Jewish without expressly saying this about Priscilla. At Corinth, they welcome Paul and work with him making tents. They travel with Paul to Ephesus, where they explain God's way more fully to Apollos. Paul calls them his helpers, and a church meets in their house. Her name appears before or after Aquila's in different passages. Second Timothy 4:19 uses Prisca.

geography.origin: Not stated; recently come from Italy (Acts 18:2)

people.name: Aquila
people.summary: A Jew born in Pontus, who arrives from Italy with Priscilla after Claudius's decree. Acts says he shares Paul's trade, and they make tents together at Corinth. He travels with Paul to Ephesus and joins Priscilla in teaching Apollos. Paul calls the pair his helpers and sends greetings “with the church that is in their house”. These passages do not give the date or circumstances of their conversion.

people.name: Gamaliel
people.summary: A Pharisee and law teacher whom Acts describes as widely respected. During the apostles' trial, he asks that they leave briefly and warns the council to act carefully. He argues that a human movement will fail, while a movement from God cannot be overthrown. Opposing it could mean fighting God. The council agrees, but has the apostles beaten and forbids speaking in Jesus' name. Paul later says Gamaliel taught him. Acts does not say this advice means Gamaliel joined the movement. He is distinct from the Gamaliel in Numbers.

linked_stories.title: The Lame Man Healed and Arrest of Peter and John

people.name: Lydia
people.summary: A seller of purple goods from Thyatira who worships God. She hears Paul at a riverside prayer gathering outside Philippi. Acts says the Lord opens her heart to his words. She and her household are baptized, and she urges Paul's group to stay at her house. After prison, Paul and Silas return there to meet and comfort the believers. The account does not state her marital status, wealth or household members' ages.

people.name: Felix
people.summary: The Roman governor to whom Paul is sent under guard from Jerusalem to Caesarea. He hears the high priest's accusation and Paul's reply. Acts describes his knowledge of the movement and his delay until Lysias can come. He and his Jewish wife Drusilla hear Paul discuss faith in Christ. Paul speaks about right conduct, self-control and coming judgment. Felix becomes afraid and sends him away. Acts 24:26 also says he hopes Paul will offer money. Two years later, Festus replaces him. Acts says Felix leaves Paul imprisoned to please the Jewish leaders.

linked_stories.title: Paul Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa

people.name: Festus
people.summary: Porcius Festus, named in Acts 24:27 as Felix's successor. Three days after arriving, he visits Jerusalem. Leaders ask him to bring Paul there, while planning an ambush. Festus holds the hearing at Caesarea. Acts says he wishes to please the leaders when he asks Paul about a Jerusalem trial. Paul appeals to Caesar. After consulting his council, Festus grants the appeal. He later presents the case to visiting King Agrippa so he can decide what to write.

linked_stories.title: Paul Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa

people.name: Agrippa
people.summary: A king whom Acts calls Agrippa, visiting Caesarea with Bernice to greet Festus. He allows Paul to speak. Paul describes his earlier life as a Pharisee, persecution of the church and vision near Damascus. Paul asks, “King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest”. Agrippa replies, “Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian”. He and Festus agree that Paul has done nothing deserving death or imprisonment. Agrippa says Paul could have been freed without his appeal to Caesar. Acts does not give the fuller historical name Herod Agrippa II in this account.

linked_stories.title: Paul Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa

people.name: Andrew
people.summary: A fisherman from Bethsaida and Peter's brother. John first presents him as a follower of John the Baptist who brings Peter to Jesus. Matthew and Mark describe Jesus calling the brothers from their fishing nets. These scenes are not combined into one sequence here. Andrew points out the boy with five barley loaves before the feeding of the crowd. With Philip, he brings Greek visitors' request to Jesus. He is one of four who ask Jesus privately about the temple's future on the Mount of Olives.

linked_stories.title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana

people.name: James son of Zebedee
people.summary: Zebedee's son, called with his brother John while they mend nets in their father's boat. They leave the boat and father to follow Jesus. Mark says Jesus names them Boanerges, sons of thunder. With Peter and John, James enters Jairus's house and sees Jesus transformed on the mountain. He and John ask for seats beside Jesus in glory, upsetting the other ten. Jesus says they will drink his cup. Luke describes them asking to call down fire after a Samaritan village refuses Jesus. Acts says King Herod kills James, John's brother, with a sword.

linked_stories.title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration in Mark

people.name: John son of Zebedee
people.summary: Zebedee's son and James's brother, called with James from their fishing boat. He joins Peter and James at Jairus's house and when Jesus is transformed on the mountain. He reports stopping a man who casts out devils in Jesus' name. With James, he requests seats beside Jesus and proposes fire against a Samaritan village. Acts places him with Peter at the temple, before the council and in Samaria. The council calls them “unlearned and ignorant men”. John's Gospel leaves the beloved disciple unnamed while saying that disciple testified and wrote these things. This profile does not identify that disciple as John or settle authorship.

linked_stories.title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration in Mark
The Lame Man Healed and Arrest of Peter and John

people.name: Matthew
people.summary: Matthew describes Jesus calling a tax collector named Matthew with “Follow me”, after which he follows. Mark describes a similar call to Levi, Alphaeus's son, while Luke names Levi. Luke says Levi leaves everything and holds a feast with tax collectors and others. Mark also places the meal at Levi's house. Matthew 10:3 names “Matthew the publican” among the Twelve; Acts includes Matthew in the upper room. The Matthew/Levi association is kept qualified here because no cited verse directly states it. Alphaeus is therefore not entered as Matthew's unqualified parent.

geography.origin: Not stated; at the receipt of custom (Matthew 9:9)

people.name: Philip the apostle
people.summary: A man from Bethsaida, also home to Andrew and Peter. John describes Jesus finding him in Galilee and saying, “Follow me”. He tells Nathanael they have found the figure Moses and the prophets wrote about. When Nathanael questions Nazareth, Philip replies, “Come and see”. Before the crowd is fed, he says two hundred pennyworth of bread would not be enough. Greek visitors approach him; he and Andrew bring their request to Jesus. At supper, he asks to see the Father. Jesus replies that seeing him means seeing the Father. Acts names him in the upper room. He is distinct from Philip the evangelist.

linked_stories.title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana

people.name: Nathanael
people.summary: Philip brings him to Jesus after saying they have found the figure described in the law and prophets. Nathanael questions whether good can come from Nazareth. John describes Jesus greeting him as an Israelite without deceit and saying he saw him under the fig tree. Nathanael replies, “Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.” John 21:2 calls him “of Cana in Galilee” among the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. The cited passages do not call him an apostle or identify him with Bartholomew.

linked_stories.title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana
Breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias

people.name: Herod the tetrarch
people.summary: Called Herod the tetrarch, ruling Galilee in Tiberius's fifteenth year. Antipas is a conventional historical label, not the KJV name. John rebukes his marriage to Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and Herod imprisons him. Mark says Herod fears John and listens gladly. At a birthday feast, he promises Herodias's daughter whatever she asks. Though sorry, he orders John's execution to keep his oath. Hearing about Jesus, he says John has risen. Luke records a warning that Herod seeks Jesus' death and Jesus calling him a fox. At trial, Herod questions and mocks Jesus, then returns him to Pilate. Luke says the two rulers become friends that day.

geography.origin: Not stated in the Gospels; tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 3:1)
residence: Jerusalem at the time of the trial (Luke 23:7)

linked_stories.title: Feeding the Five Thousand and Walking on Water

people.name: Herodias
people.summary: Herod the tetrarch's wife, described in the Gospels as previously married to his brother Philip. John tells Herod that this marriage is unlawful. Mark says Herodias wants John killed but cannot while Herod protects him. At Herod's birthday feast, her daughter dances and receives a promise of whatever she requests. Herodias tells her to ask for John's head. The daughter brings it to her mother on a platter. The Gospels leave the daughter unnamed; no fuller family tree is added here.

linked_stories.title: Feeding the Five Thousand and Walking on Water

people.name: Joseph of Arimathaea
people.summary: A man from Arimathaea, distinct from Mary's husband and the patriarch Joseph. Matthew calls him rich; John describes him as a secret disciple who fears the Jewish leaders. Mark calls him a respected council member awaiting God's kingdom. Luke says he did not agree with the council's actions. Mark describes him boldly asking Pilate for Jesus' body, which Pilate grants after checking that Jesus is dead. Matthew says he wraps it in clean linen and places it in his own new rock-cut tomb. John describes Nicodemus bringing myrrh and aloes and both men wrapping the body with these substances.

geography.origin: Arimathaea (Matthew 27:57; Luke 23:51 'a city of the Jews')

linked_stories.title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial in Mark

people.name: Barabbas
people.summary: A prisoner offered for release during the feast. Matthew calls him notable. Mark links him with rebels who committed murder; Luke names revolt and murder; John calls him a robber. These descriptions remain attributed to their Gospels and do not establish different identities. Matthew describes the priests urging the crowd to choose Barabbas and demand Jesus' death. Pilate asks what wrong Jesus has done, then releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over for crucifixion. The accounts give no later biography for Barabbas.

linked_stories.title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial in Mark

people.name: Annas
people.summary: Named with Caiaphas as high priest in Luke when John begins receiving God's word. John says Jesus is first brought to Annas, Caiaphas's father-in-law, after his arrest. It then describes “the high priest” questioning Jesus about his followers and teaching. Jesus says he spoke openly, and an officer strikes him. John says Annas sent Jesus bound to Caiaphas. The passage names both men without settling the questioner's identity here. Acts again calls Annas high priest when Peter and John face the rulers. Caiaphas, John, Alexander and others from the high priest's family are also present.

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: A Jerusalem believer whose wife is Sapphira, distinct from the Damascus disciple and the high priest named Ananias. Acts says the couple sell property and knowingly keep part of the price while bringing the rest to the apostles. Peter says both land and money had been theirs to use freely. He accuses Ananias of lying to God. The account says Ananias falls down dead and fear spreads among those who hear. Young men wrap and bury him.

residence: Jerusalem (implied by Acts 5:1-2, the apostles' feet)

people.name: Sapphira
people.summary: Ananias's wife, who knows about the plan to keep part of the land's price. Acts says she comes in about three hours later, unaware of what has happened. Peter separately asks her whether the land sold for the stated amount, and she says yes. He asks why they agreed to test the Lord's Spirit. He says the men who buried her husband are at the door. Acts describes her falling dead at Peter's feet and being buried beside her husband.

people.name: Ananias of Damascus
aliases: Ananias, a devout man according to the law
people.summary: A disciple at Damascus, distinct from Sapphira's husband and the high priest. Acts 9 describes the Lord sending him in a vision to Judas's house on Straight Street. Saul is praying there and has seen Ananias coming to lay a hand on him. Ananias objects, citing Saul's persecution and authority to arrest believers. The Lord's reply describes Saul as chosen to speak before non-Jews, kings and Israel. Ananias goes, lays hands on Saul and calls him brother. He says he was sent for Saul's sight and filling with the Holy Spirit. In Paul's later account, Ananias follows the law and is respected by local Jews.

people.name: Simon the sorcerer
people.summary: A man in Samaria whom Acts describes as using sorcery and presenting himself as great. People call him God's great power. After Philip preaches, Simon believes, is baptized and follows him, amazed by the signs. Acts describes Peter and John laying hands on people, who receive the Holy Spirit. Simon offers money for that power. Peter rebukes him and tells him to turn from his wrongdoing and pray. Simon asks them to pray that the threatened harm will not happen. Acts gives no later biography. Magus is a conventional label, not his name in the KJV; he is distinct from Peter and Simon the tanner.

people.name: Dorcas
people.summary: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, is a disciple in Joppa whom Acts describes as generous and active in helping others. She becomes ill, dies and is laid in an upstairs room. Two men ask Peter to come from nearby Lydda. Widows show him clothing she made and weep. Acts describes Peter clearing the room, kneeling to pray and saying, “Tabitha, arise”. She opens her eyes and sits up, and he presents her alive to the believers and widows. The account says many in Joppa believe after hearing this.

people.name: Eutychus
people.summary: A young man present at Troas, sitting in an upstairs window while Paul speaks until midnight before leaving. Acts says he falls deeply asleep, falls from the third floor and is taken up dead. Paul goes down, embraces him and says his life is in him. Paul returns upstairs, breaks bread and talks until dawn. The account describes Eutychus being brought in alive, greatly comforting the group. It does not establish his beliefs from attendance or explain a medical mechanism.

people.name: Demetrius the silversmith
people.summary: A silversmith in Ephesus who makes silver shrines for Diana. Acts records him warning other craftspeople that Paul's teaching threatens their income and the goddess's temple. He says Paul teaches that handmade gods are not gods. The workers shout, “Great is Diana of the Ephesians”, and confusion spreads through the city. The town clerk calms the crowd. He says the accused men neither rob temples nor insult their goddess, and directs complaints to the courts. This profile covers the silversmith in Acts, without identifying him with the Demetrius in 3 John.

people.name: Claudius Lysias
people.summary: The Roman commander at Jerusalem, distinct from Emperor Claudius. Acts describes him rescuing Paul from a crowd and binding him with two chains. He asks whether Paul is the Egyptian rebel; Paul replies that he is a Jew from Tarsus. The officer orders a whipping to question Paul but draws back on learning Paul is Roman. He says he bought citizenship, while Paul says he was born with it. After Paul's nephew reports an ambush plot, he sends Paul to Felix at Caesarea under a large guard. His letter names him and says Paul has done nothing deserving death or imprisonment. Those assessments remain the officer's claims.

geography.origin: Not stated; he bought Roman citizenship (Acts 22:28)

people.name: Luke
people.summary: Paul's companion named in three letters. Philemon calls Lucas a fellow worker; Colossians calls Luke “the beloved physician”; Second Timothy says only Luke is with Paul. The last passage does not establish a final imprisonment. Acts never names Luke, though its narration changes to “we” in parts of the journeys. Acts addresses Theophilus and refers to “The former treatise”; Luke's Gospel also addresses Theophilus. The traditional link between these books, Luke and the unnamed travelling narrator is not an explicit statement of the texts.

residence: Not stated in the cited letters.

record.title: Noah
record.summary: Described as doing what is right and walking with God, Noah brings his family into the ark through the flood. God’s covenant, or binding agreement, afterward promises no further flood to destroy all flesh. It gives the rainbow as its sign. His later drunkenness leads into the story in which he curses Canaan.

meaning.original: Described as righteous and walking with God, Noah brings his family into the ark through the flood. God’s covenant afterward promises no further flood to destroy all flesh and gives the rainbow as its sign. His later drunkenness leads into the episode in which he curses Canaan.
meaningChecks: Kept the scope “all flesh” and the covenant as a binding agreement; “promise” alone could narrow its meaning.

record.title: Japheth
record.summary: Noah’s son who survives the flood with his wife. He and Shem cover their father without looking at his nakedness. Noah’s words that follow ask God to enlarge Japheth and connect his future with Shem’s tents.

meaning.original: Noah’s son who survives the flood with his wife. He and Shem cover their father while avoiding looking at his nakedness. Noah’s ensuing words ask God to enlarge Japheth and connect his future with Shem’s tents.
meaningChecks: Kept “enlarge Japheth” and “Shem’s tents”: choosing population, territory or another meaning would add an interpretation.

record.title: Abraham
record.summary: Also called Abram; he receives promises of land, descendants and blessing for the families of the earth. The story of the covenant, or binding agreement, introduces circumcision, the removal of the foreskin. It identifies Isaac as Sarah’s promised son. Abraham’s willingness to offer Isaac becomes a central test, stopped before the child is killed.

meaning.original: Also called Abram; the recipient of promises of land, descendants and blessing for the families of the earth. The covenant narrative introduces circumcision and identifies Isaac as Sarah’s promised son. Abraham’s willingness to offer Isaac becomes a central test, stopped before the child is killed.
meaningChecks: Kept covenant and circumcision, with short word definitions. “Promise” or “ceremony” alone would lose their meaning.

record.title: Sarah
record.summary: Also called Sarai; Abraham’s wife and the mother of Isaac, born in their old age as the promised covenant child. A covenant is a binding agreement. Abraham also identifies her as his half-sister through their father. Her conflict with Hagar and demand that Hagar and Ishmael leave shape the story of the household’s inheritance.

meaning.original: Also called Sarai; Abraham’s wife and the mother of Isaac, born in their old age as the promised covenant child. Abraham also identifies her as his paternal half-sister. Her conflict with Hagar and demand that Hagar and Ishmael leave shape the household’s inheritance story.
meaningChecks: Kept the promised covenant child and the shared father in the half-sister claim.

record.title: Rebekah
record.summary: Bethuel’s daughter and Laban’s sister, who agrees to leave her family and marry Isaac. An oracle about her twins says the older will serve the younger. An oracle is a message said to come from a god. She later helps Jacob gain Isaac’s blessing by disguising him as Esau.

meaning.original: Bethuel’s daughter and Laban’s sister, who agrees to leave her family and marry Isaac. An oracle about her twins says the elder will serve the younger. She later helps Jacob obtain Isaac’s blessing by disguising him as Esau.
meaningChecks: Kept oracle with a brief word definition, without naming the speaker or adding content to the message about the twins.

record.title: Reuben
record.summary: Jacob and Leah’s firstborn, who steps in to stop his brothers from killing Joseph. He also sleeps with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, a partner with lower status than a wife. Jacob’s final words clearly connect that act with Reuben’s loss of first place.

meaning.original: Jacob and Leah’s firstborn, who intervenes to stop his brothers from killing Joseph. He also sleeps with Bilhah, his father’s concubine. Jacob’s final words explicitly connect that act with Reuben’s loss of preeminence.
meaningChecks: Kept concubine with a brief status definition; calling Bilhah simply a wife would erase the source distinction.

record.title: Simeon
record.summary: Jacob and Leah’s son, who joins Levi in killing the men of Shechem after Dinah’s violation. Jacob later condemns their violent anger and says they will be scattered. In the Joseph story, Simeon is held in Egypt while his brothers return for Benjamin.

meaning.original: Jacob and Leah’s son, who joins Levi in killing the men of Shechem after Dinah’s violation. Jacob later condemns their violent anger and announces their scattering. In the Joseph narrative, Simeon is held in Egypt while his brothers return for Benjamin.
meaningChecks: Retained “violation” because a more specific description would add detail not given by this summary.

record.title: Levi
record.summary: Jacob and Leah’s son, who joins Simeon in the attack on Shechem after Dinah’s violation. Jacob’s final words condemn their violent anger and speak of their scattering in Israel. He is the named ancestor of the Levi family line, one of the ancestors of Israel’s tribes.

meaning.original: Jacob and Leah’s son, who joins Simeon in the attack on Shechem after Dinah’s violation. Jacob’s final words condemn their violent anger and speak of their scattering in Israel. He is the named ancestor of the Levi family line, one of Israel’s tribal ancestors.
meaningChecks: Retained “violation” because a more specific description would add detail not given by this summary.

record.title: Dinah
record.summary: Jacob and Leah’s daughter, whose violation by Shechem leads to talks about marriage. It also leads to a deadly response by her brothers Simeon and Levi. Their attack and Jacob’s reaction make her story central to the family’s conflict with Shechem.

meaning.original: Jacob and Leah’s daughter, whose violation by Shechem leads to marriage negotiations and a deadly response by her brothers Simeon and Levi. Their attack and Jacob’s reaction make her story central to the family’s conflict with Shechem.
meaningChecks: Retained “violation” because a more specific description would add detail not given by this summary.

record.title: Paul
record.summary: Also called Saul, he persecutes Jesus’ followers before becoming someone who testifies about Jesus. He becomes a missionary to Gentiles, or non-Jews. A missionary spreads a faith. Acts follows his work as a missionary and his time in prison through his arrival in Rome. His letters identify him as an apostle, a messenger sent with authority. They address the inclusion of Gentiles, faith and the law, the resurrection, and the life of communities he writes to. Resurrection means rising from the dead.

meaning.original: Also called Saul, a persecutor of Jesus’ followers who becomes a witness to Jesus and a missionary to the Gentiles. Acts follows his missionary work and imprisonment through his arrival in Rome. His letters identify him as an apostle and address Gentile inclusion, faith and the law, the resurrection, and the life of the communities he writes to.
meaningChecks: Testifies about Jesus preserves the nontechnical sense of witness without adding a claim that Paul saw a particular event. Other role terms receive brief definitions.

record.title: Elisha
record.summary: Shaphat’s son from Abel-meholah, called from plowing to follow Elijah. After taking up Elijah’s cloak, he is recognized as the one to take Elijah’s place. His stories include providing for a widow, restoring a child to life, and Naaman’s healing. They also include a curse followed by bears mauling forty-two mockers. He also steps into royal affairs and sends a prophet to anoint Jehu, marking his appointment with oil.

meaning.original: Shaphat’s son from Abel-meholah, called from plowing to follow Elijah and recognized as his successor after taking up his mantle. His stories include provision for a widow, restoring a child to life, Naaman’s healing, and a curse followed by bears mauling forty-two mockers. He also intervenes in royal affairs and sends a prophet to anoint Jehu.
meaningChecks: Preserved the order “curse followed by bears” without adding a causal claim; retained forty-two.

record.title: Aaron
record.summary: Moses’ older brother and spokesman, appointed with his sons to serve as priests. While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes the golden calf and declares a feast. This makes him central to that break with proper worship. Like Moses he is barred from entering Canaan after Meribah. His priestly clothes pass to Eleazar before he dies on Mount Hor.

meaning.original: Moses’ older brother and spokesman, appointed with his sons to the priestly office. While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes the golden calf and proclaims a feast, making him central to that breach of worship. Like Moses he is barred from entering Canaan after Meribah; his priestly garments pass to Eleazar before he dies on Mount Hor.
meaningChecks: “Break with proper worship” retains the source’s judgment about worship; it does not identify a new rule.

record.title: Miriam
record.summary: Moses and Aaron’s sister, identified as a female prophet. She leads the women in song and dance after the sea crossing. She and Aaron later challenge Moses. The account describes her getting leprosy, Moses praying for her healing, and the camp waiting through her seven-day exclusion. She dies and is buried at Kadesh.

meaning.original: Moses and Aaron’s sister, identified as a prophetess who leads the women in song and dance after the sea crossing. She and Aaron later challenge Moses; the account describes her becoming leprous, Moses praying for her healing, and the camp waiting through her seven-day exclusion. She dies and is buried at Kadesh.
meaningChecks: “Leprosy” restates “leprous” as the account’s description, not a modern medical diagnosis.

record.title: The Fall of Man
record.summary: The serpent persuades the woman to eat from the forbidden tree, and the man also eats. God confronts them, states what will follow, and sends them out of Eden. The serpent challenges the warning about the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. After eating, the pair recognize their nakedness, make coverings and hide. Each is questioned, and the man and woman shift responsibility. The account describes pain, hard work and death. God clothes them. He then places cherubim and a flaming sword at the garden's entrance to guard the tree of life.

meaning.original: The serpent persuades the woman to eat from the forbidden tree, and the man also eats. God confronts them, announces consequences, and sends them out of Eden. The serpent challenges the warning about the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. After eating, the pair recognize their nakedness, make coverings and hide. Each is questioned, and the man and woman shift responsibility. The account describes pain, difficult labor and mortality. God clothes them before placing cherubim and a flaming sword at the garden's entrance to guard the tree of life.
meaningChecks: Kept cherubim as the source’s name for the guards. Replacing them with angels or adding a physical description would add detail.

record.title: Noah and the Flood
record.summary: Noah builds an ark to save his household and animals through the flood. Afterward, God makes a binding agreement with Noah and living creatures, with the rainbow as its sign. The earth is described as corrupt and filled with violence. Noah follows instructions for the ark and enters with his family and animals. Rain and rising waters cover the land; later, Noah sends birds to seek signs of dry ground. He leaves the ark and builds an altar. God's agreement promises that a flood will not again destroy all flesh. It sets the bow in the clouds as its reminder.

meaning.original: Noah builds an ark to preserve his household and animals through the flood. Afterward, God establishes a covenant with Noah and living creatures, with the rainbow as its sign. The earth is described as corrupt and filled with violence. Noah follows instructions for the ark and enters with his family and animals. Rain and rising waters cover the land; later, Noah sends birds to seek signs of dry ground. He leaves the ark and builds an altar. God's covenant promises that a flood will not again destroy all flesh, and sets the bow in the clouds as its reminder.
meaningChecks: Covenant becomes binding agreement; the promise still concerns all flesh, not an end to every flood.

record.title: Abraham and Sarah’s Covenant
record.summary: Abram and Sarai receive the names Abraham and Sarah. God promises a son named Isaac, and visitors announce his coming birth. God makes circumcision, the removal of the foreskin, the sign of the covenant, or binding agreement. He promises Sarah a son despite her age. Abraham asks about Ishmael, who is also promised descendants, but the agreement is to continue through Isaac. Abraham circumcises the males of his household. Later, he welcomes three visitors as guests. Sarah overhears their promise and laughs within herself. She is challenged with the question of whether anything is too hard for the Lord.

meaning.original: Abram and Sarai receive the names Abraham and Sarah. God promises a son named Isaac, and visitors announce his coming birth. God establishes circumcision as the covenant's sign and promises Sarah a son despite her age. Abraham asks about Ishmael, who is also promised descendants, but the covenant is to continue through Isaac. Abraham circumcises the males of his household. Later, three visitors receive his hospitality. Sarah overhears their promise, laughs within herself and is challenged with the question of whether anything is too hard for the Lord.
meaningChecks: Kept covenant and circumcision with word definitions; replacing them with promise or ceremony would lose meaning.

record.title: Dinah at Shechem
record.summary: Shechem violates Dinah and seeks to marry her. Her brothers Simeon and Levi attack the city, and Jacob fears others will strike back. Shechem's father Hamor proposes marriages between the households. Dinah's brothers give a false answer. They require the city's males to be circumcised, having their foreskins removed. While the men recover, Simeon and Levi kill them, including Hamor and Shechem, and bring Dinah out. The other brothers loot the city and take captives. Jacob objects that the attack has put his household at risk among the surrounding peoples. His sons answer by pointing to Dinah's treatment.

meaning.original: Shechem violates Dinah and seeks to marry her. Her brothers Simeon and Levi attack the city, and Jacob fears retaliation. Shechem's father Hamor proposes intermarriage between the households. Dinah's brothers answer deceitfully, requiring the city's males to be circumcised. While the men recover, Simeon and Levi kill them, including Hamor and Shechem, and bring Dinah out. The other brothers plunder the city and take captives. Jacob objects that the attack has endangered his household among the surrounding peoples; his sons answer by pointing to Dinah's treatment.
meaningChecks: Kept “violates” without making the sexual violence more specific than the source. Circumcision receives a brief word definition.

record.title: The Death of Rachel
record.summary: Jacob returns to Bethel. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and the chapter lists Jacob’s twelve sons and tells of Isaac’s death. Jacob tells his household to put away foreign gods before traveling to Bethel, where he builds an altar. God repeats the name Israel and the promise of descendants and land. Rachel goes into hard labor on the journey and dies after giving birth to her second son. Jacob calls him Benjamin and marks her grave. The chapter also records Reuben's act with Bilhah. It tells of Isaac's burial by Esau and Jacob.

meaning.original: Jacob returns to Bethel. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and the chapter lists Jacob’s twelve sons and recounts Isaac’s death. Jacob instructs his household to put away foreign gods before traveling to Bethel, where he builds an altar. God repeats the name Israel and the promise of descendants and land. Rachel goes into hard labor on the journey and dies after giving birth to her second son. Jacob calls him Benjamin and marks her grave. The chapter also records Reuben's act with Bilhah and the burial of Isaac by Esau and Jacob.
meaningChecks: Kept the source’s unspecific “Reuben’s act with Bilhah”; naming an act would add a claim to this summary.

record.title: Moses Returns to Egypt
record.summary: Moses leaves Midian with his family and the staff of God. During a dangerous encounter with the LORD on the journey, Zipporah circumcises her son by removing his foreskin. Aaron meets Moses, and the people of Israel believe the signs. After getting his father-in-law's permission, Moses sets out. God tells him that those seeking his life are dead. God also warns that Pharaoh will resist and calls Israel his firstborn son. Following the encounter on the road, Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God. Together they gather Israel's elders, pass on the message and perform the signs. The people bow in worship on hearing that God has seen their suffering.

meaning.original: Moses leaves Midian with his family and the staff of God. During a dangerous encounter with the LORD on the journey, Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets Moses, and the people of Israel believe the signs. After obtaining his father-in-law's permission, Moses sets out, and God tells him that those seeking his life are dead. God also warns that Pharaoh will resist and calls Israel his firstborn son. Following the encounter on the road, Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God. Together they gather Israel's elders, relay the message and perform the signs. The people bow in worship on hearing that God has seen their affliction.
meaningChecks: Kept the dangerous encounter with the LORD unspecified. The circumcision wording defines the act without adding a reason for it.

record.title: The Passover and the Death of the Firstborn
record.summary: God announces the death of Egypt's firstborn and gives Israel the Passover instructions. These call for a lamb, blood on the doorposts, and bread made without leaven. Leaven makes dough rise. At midnight the firstborn die, and Pharaoh sends Israel out as Egyptians give them silver, gold and clothing. Households are instructed to eat the meal ready to depart and to remember the event in future generations. Moses warns that a great cry will rise through Egypt, while Israel is to be protected. After the deaths, Pharaoh calls Moses and Aaron during the night. He tells them to go with their people and flocks. The departing Israelites carry dough before it has been leavened, or made to rise.

meaning.original: God announces the death of Egypt's firstborn and gives Israel the Passover instructions: a lamb, blood on the doorposts, and unleavened bread. At midnight the firstborn die, and Pharaoh sends Israel out as Egyptians give them silver, gold and clothing. Households are instructed to eat the meal ready to depart and to remember the event in future generations. Moses warns that a great cry will rise through Egypt, while Israel is to be protected. After the deaths, Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron during the night and tells them to go with their people and flocks. The departing Israelites carry dough before it has been leavened.
meaningChecks: Kept leaven and leavened with short explanations. Substituting yeast would narrow the term; the draft does not add an ingredient or method.

record.title: The Exodus from Egypt
record.summary: Israel leaves Rameses, taking the bones of Joseph, with the firstborn set apart for the LORD. A pillar of cloud by day and fire by night guides the people. The departure includes a mixed crowd and livestock. Instructions link bread made without leaven and dedicating firstborn offspring with remembering rescue from slavery. Leaven makes dough rise. The route avoids the nearer way through the land of the Philistines. The people might turn back if faced with war. Moses carries Joseph's bones to fulfill the earlier oath, and the guiding pillars remain before the travelers.

meaning.original: Israel leaves Rameses, taking the bones of Joseph, with the firstborn consecrated to the LORD. A pillar of cloud by day and fire by night guides the people. The departure includes a mixed multitude and livestock. Instructions connect unleavened bread and the dedication of firstborn offspring with remembering deliverance from slavery. The route avoids the nearer way through the land of the Philistines because the people might turn back if faced with war. Moses carries Joseph's bones in fulfillment of the earlier oath, and the guiding pillars remain before the travelers.
meaningChecks: Kept leaven with a short explanation instead of narrowing it to yeast. The firstborn dedication remains linked to remembering rescue from slavery.

record.title: The Blasphemer Stoned
record.summary: The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man curses the Name in a fight. After the LORD is consulted, the gathered people stone him. The rule of equal justice for native people and those staying among them is stated again.

meaning.original: The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man curses the Name in a fight. After the LORD is consulted, the congregation stones him, and the principle of equal justice for native and sojourner is restated.
meaningChecks: Kept “the Name” as the original designation; adding a divine name would add specificity. Sojourner becomes someone staying among native people.

record.title: Offerings and the Passover at Sinai
record.summary: The tribal leaders bring offerings for the altar, and the Levites are set apart. Israel keeps the Passover, with a later date allowed for those unclean under ritual rules. The cloud over the tabernacle, the sacred tent, signals when to move or camp.

meaning.original: The tribal leaders present offerings for the altar, the Levites are set apart, and Israel keeps the Passover, with a later date allowed for those unclean. The cloud over the tabernacle signals when to move or camp.
meaningChecks: Unclean refers to ritual status; replacing it with dirty or sick would change the stated limit.

record.title: The Bronze Serpent
record.summary: The people speak against God and Moses, and fiery snakes bite them. Moses makes a bronze snake on a pole, and those who look at it live.

meaning.original: The people speak against God and Moses, and fiery serpents bite them. Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole, and those who look at it live.
meaningChecks: Kept “fiery” rather than deciding whether it means burning pain, color or another feature.

record.title: Balaam and Balak
record.summary: Balak of Moab hires Balaam to curse Israel. Balaam's donkey sees the angel of the LORD, and Balaam blesses Israel instead. He ends with oracles about a star out of Jacob. Oracles are messages said to come from a god.

meaning.original: Balak of Moab hires Balaam to curse Israel. Balaam's donkey sees the angel of the LORD, and Balaam blesses Israel instead, ending with oracles about a star out of Jacob.
meaningChecks: Kept oracles with a brief word definition, without naming a speaker or interpreting the star.

record.title: Moses Recalls the Second Tablets
record.summary: Moses recalls making an ark, a sacred chest, and two stone tablets, then going up the mountain. He recalls placing the tablets written by the LORD inside the ark. He also recalls his pleading for others and the command to lead the people onward.

meaning.original: Moses recalls making an ark and two stone tablets, going up the mountain, and placing the tablets written by the LORD inside the ark. He also recalls his intercession and the command to lead the people onward.
meaningChecks: Ark is explained as a sacred chest here; treating it as Noah’s boat would change the object.

record.title: Joshua Commissioned and the Law Entrusted
record.summary: Moses tells Israel that Joshua will lead them across the Jordan and encourages Joshua before the people. He gives the written law to the priests and appears with Joshua at the tabernacle, the sacred tent. He writes and teaches a song to serve as evidence for Israel.

meaning.original: Moses tells Israel that Joshua will lead them across the Jordan and encourages Joshua before the people. He delivers the written law to the priests, appears with Joshua at the tabernacle, and writes and teaches a song as a witness for Israel.
meaningChecks: Witness describes the song’s role as evidence, not an ancient copy. Kept “for Israel” without specifying a charge or outcome.

record.title: The Fall of Jericho
record.summary: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days, and on the seventh day the walls fall at the shout. The city is set apart for destruction; Rahab and her family are spared.

meaning.original: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days, and on the seventh day the walls fall at the shout. The city is devoted to destruction; Rahab and her family are spared.
meaningChecks: Kept “set apart for destruction”; simply saying the city is destroyed would lose the source’s designation.

record.title: Achan's Sin and Ai
record.summary: Achan takes goods set apart at Jericho, and Israel is defeated at Ai. After Achan is identified and stoned, Israel takes Ai by ambush and renews the binding agreement at Ebal and Gerizim.

meaning.original: Achan takes devoted goods from Jericho, and Israel is defeated at Ai. After Achan is identified and stoned, Israel takes Ai by ambush and renews the covenant at Ebal and Gerizim.
meaningChecks: Devoted goods becomes goods set apart; the draft does not choose a purpose beyond what this summary states.

record.title: The Altar by the Jordan
record.summary: The eastern tribes build a large altar by the Jordan, and the western tribes prepare for war. A group sent with Phinehas as its leader hears that the altar serves as evidence, not a place for sacrifice. The matter is settled.

meaning.original: The eastern tribes build a large altar by the Jordan, and the western tribes prepare for war. A delegation led by Phinehas hears that it is a witness, not a place for sacrifice, and the matter is settled.
meaningChecks: Witness becomes evidence. The original does not say here what the altar proves, so the draft does not add an object.

record.title: Samson
record.summary: Born to a woman unable to have children, Samson is set apart as a Nazirite, someone under a special vow. He fights the Philistines. Betrayed by Delilah, he loses his hair, is blinded, and brings down a temple on himself and many Philistines.

meaning.original: Born to a barren woman and set apart as a Nazirite, Samson fights the Philistines. Betrayed by Delilah, he loses his hair, is blinded, and brings down a temple on himself and many Philistines.
meaningChecks: Nazirite receives only a short word definition; the draft does not invent the terms of the vow.

record.title: The Levite and Gibeah
record.summary: A Levite’s concubine, a partner with lower status than a wife, is abused to death at Gibeah of Benjamin. Israel goes to war against Benjamin, nearly wipes it out, and then arranges wives for the survivors.

meaning.original: A Levite's concubine is abused to death at Gibeah of Benjamin. Israel goes to war against Benjamin, nearly wipes it out, and then arranges wives for the survivors.
meaningChecks: Kept concubine with a brief status definition; “wife” alone would erase the source distinction.

record.title: The Threshing Floor
record.summary: On Naomi's advice Ruth lies at Boaz's feet at the place where grain is separated from stalks. Boaz promises to act as redeemer, buying back on the family’s behalf, if a closer relative declines.

meaning.original: On Naomi's advice Ruth lies at Boaz's feet at the threshing floor. Boaz promises to act as redeemer if a nearer kinsman declines.
meaningChecks: Redeemer is retained with a brief word explanation. The draft does not add an object to buy back, marriage terms or the relative’s decision.

record.title: Saul and the Medium at Endor; Saul's Death
record.summary: Saul consults a medium, someone who seeks contact with the dead, at Endor and is told he will die. David is sent away from the Philistine army and defeats the Amalekites at Ziklag. Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa.

meaning.original: Saul consults a medium at Endor and is told he will die. David is dismissed from the Philistine army and defeats the Amalekites at Ziklag; Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa.
meaningChecks: Medium receives a word definition describing the role; it does not add a claim about whether contact succeeds.

record.title: The Davidic Covenant
record.summary: David wishes to build a house for the LORD. But through Nathan God promises to build David a house and make his throne last forever.

meaning.original: David wishes to build a house for the LORD, but through Nathan God promises to build David a house and establish his throne forever.
meaningChecks: Kept both uses of house without selecting a building or family-line interpretation beyond this summary.

record.title: The Man of God from Judah
record.summary: A man of God from Judah gives a prophecy against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel. He then disobeys and is killed by a lion. Ahijah announces the end of Jeroboam's house.

meaning.original: A man of God from Judah prophesies against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, then disobeys and is killed by a lion. Ahijah announces the end of Jeroboam's house.
meaningChecks: Kept prophecy without supplying its content, source or outcome beyond this record.

record.title: The Death of Saul
record.summary: Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa. The writer says Saul died for his unfaithfulness, including consulting a medium, someone who seeks contact with the dead.

meaning.original: Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa, and the chronicler says Saul died for his unfaithfulness, including consulting a medium.
meaningChecks: Kept the explanation attributed to the writer. The definition of medium describes a role, not a verified ability.

record.title: Cyrus's Decree and the Return
record.summary: Cyrus of Persia allows the Jews to return and rebuild the temple and returns the temple containers. A list records those who go back under Zerubbabel and Jeshua.

meaning.original: Cyrus of Persia authorizes the Jews to return and rebuild the temple and returns the temple vessels. A list records those who go back under Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
meaningChecks: Vessels becomes containers; the draft does not specify materials or types absent from this summary.

record.title: Opposition and Delay
record.summary: Opponents offer to help rebuild the temple, are refused, and block the work. The chapter also tells of later letters that lead Artaxerxes to stop work on Jerusalem’s city. It closes by returning to the temple work halted until Darius’s rule.

meaning.original: Opponents offer to help rebuild the temple, are refused, and obstruct the work. The chapter also recounts later letters that lead Artaxerxes to stop work on Jerusalem’s city; it closes by returning to the temple work halted until Darius’s reign.
meaningChecks: Preserved the switch from temple work to later city letters and back; these are not collapsed into one project.

record.title: Isaiah's Call
record.summary: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the LORD on a throne. A seraph touches his lips with a coal. He is sent to a people who will not understand.

meaning.original: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the LORD on a throne and a seraph touches his lips with a coal. He is sent to a people who will not understand.
meaningChecks: Kept seraph as the source’s name for the figure. Substituting angel or describing its form would add detail absent here.

record.title: Ahaz and the Sign of Immanuel
record.summary: Syria and Israel threaten Judah. Isaiah tells King Ahaz to stand firm. When Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign, Isaiah announces that a virgin will become pregnant. She will bear a son called Immanuel.

meaning.original: Syria and Israel threaten Judah. Isaiah tells King Ahaz to stand firm, and when Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign, Isaiah announces that a virgin shall conceive and bear a son called Immanuel.
meaningChecks: Kept virgin exactly as the record’s claim; the draft does not substitute a different reading or add interpretation.

record.title: Hananiah's False Prophecy
record.summary: Hananiah breaks the yoke, a frame for carrying a load, that Jeremiah wears. He says Babylon's rule will end in two years. Jeremiah answers that the yoke will be iron, and Hananiah dies that year.

meaning.original: Hananiah breaks the yoke Jeremiah wears and says Babylon's rule will end in two years. Jeremiah answers that the yoke will be iron, and Hananiah dies that year.
meaningChecks: Yoke receives a brief word definition; the draft does not specify its material or interpret the sign. Two years is unchanged.

record.title: Jeremiah in the Cistern
record.summary: During the army’s blockade, Jeremiah is arrested and lowered into a muddy cistern, a pit for storing water. Ebed-melech the Cushite pulls him out, and Zedekiah consults him in private.

meaning.original: During the siege Jeremiah is arrested and lowered into a muddy cistern. Ebed-melech the Cushite pulls him out, and Zedekiah consults him privately.
meaningChecks: Siege becomes an army’s blockade; the draft does not name an army or place. Cistern receives a word definition.

record.title: Ezekiel's Vision and Commission
record.summary: By the Chebar canal Ezekiel sees four living creatures and wheels. He is given a scroll to eat and is made a lookout for Israel.

meaning.original: By the Chebar canal Ezekiel sees four living creatures and wheels, is given a scroll to eat, and is made a watchman for Israel.
meaningChecks: Watchman becomes lookout; the draft does not add duties or interpret the vision.

record.title: The Death of Ezekiel's Wife
record.summary: The LORD tells Ezekiel that the desire of his eyes will be taken away. He commands him not to perform the usual acts of mourning. His wife dies that evening. He explains his actions to the people as a sign about the sacred place and their families.

meaning.original: The LORD tells Ezekiel that the desire of his eyes will be taken away and commands him not to perform the usual mourning rites. His wife dies that evening; he explains his conduct to the people as a sign concerning the sanctuary and their families.
meaningChecks: Kept “desire of his eyes” without adding a paraphrase of the metaphor; no reason for the death is added.

record.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Statue
record.summary: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell him both his dream and its meaning. God reveals it to Daniel. A stone strikes a statue of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay. Daniel explains this as God’s kingdom defeating the kingdoms shown by the statue.

meaning.original: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell him both his dream and its interpretation. God reveals it to Daniel: a statue of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay is struck by a stone, which Daniel interprets as God’s kingdom overcoming the kingdoms represented by the statue.
meaningChecks: Kept the kingdom explanation attributed to Daniel; all five materials remain.

record.title: Daniel's Visions
record.summary: Daniel sees four beasts and a son of man, a ram and a goat. He receives the answer to prayer about seventy weeks and a final vision of kings and the end.

meaning.original: Daniel sees four beasts and a son of man, a ram and a goat, and receives the prayer-answer about seventy weeks and a final vision of kings and the end.
meaningChecks: Kept seventy weeks without converting it to years or interpreting the end.

record.title: The Birth of Jesus and the Magi
record.summary: Joseph learns in a dream that Mary's child is from the Holy Spirit. Magi, or wise men, follow a star to Bethlehem and bring gifts to the child.

meaning.original: Joseph learns in a dream that Mary's child is from the Holy Spirit. Magi follow a star to Bethlehem and bring gifts to the child.
meaningChecks: Magi is retained with the broad equivalent wise men; no number, origin or occupation is added.

record.title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration
record.summary: Peter says Jesus is the Christ, and Jesus foretells his death and rising from the dead. Six days later his appearance is changed before Peter, James and John.

meaning.original: Peter says Jesus is the Christ, and Jesus foretells his death and resurrection. Six days later he is transfigured before Peter, James and John.
meaningChecks: Kept Christ as the source’s title without adding a definition of the expected role. Transfigured becomes appearance changed, with no description added.

record.title: Calling the Disciples and Healing in Capernaum
record.summary: Jesus calls four fishermen and drives out an unclean spirit in the synagogue, a Jewish place of worship. He heals Peter's mother-in-law and makes a person with leprosy clean.

meaning.original: Jesus calls four fishermen, casts out an unclean spirit in the synagogue, heals Peter's mother-in-law and cleanses a leper.
meaningChecks: Kept the source’s distinction between healing and making clean; “unclean spirit” remains the record’s description.

record.title: The Gadarene Demoniac, Jairus and the Woman
record.summary: Jesus sends a legion, a large group, of demons into pigs. He heals a woman who touched his cloak and brings Jairus's daughter back to life.

meaning.original: Jesus sends a legion of demons into pigs, heals a woman who touched his cloak, and raises Jairus's daughter.
meaningChecks: Kept legion with a broad definition; no exact size is supplied.

record.title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration in Mark
record.summary: Peter calls Jesus the Christ, and Jesus foretells his suffering. His appearance changes on a mountain and then heals a boy with an unclean spirit.

meaning.original: Peter calls Jesus the Christ, and Jesus foretells his suffering. He is transfigured on a mountain and then heals a boy with an unclean spirit.
meaningChecks: Kept Christ as a title and unclean spirit as the source’s term; the changed appearance is not given added features.

record.title: Triumphal Entry and the Temple
record.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a colt, a young riding animal, and curses a fig tree. He drives out the temple traders and is challenged on his authority.

meaning.original: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a colt, curses a fig tree, drives out the temple traders, and is challenged on his authority.
meaningChecks: Kept colt without specifying donkey or horse, which this summary does not do.

record.title: Jesus at the Feast of Dedication
record.summary: At the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, Jesus is asked whether he is the Christ. Some take up stones after his answer and try to seize him. But he escapes and goes beyond Jordan, where many believe in him.

meaning.original: At the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, Jesus is asked whether he is the Christ. Some take up stones after his answer and try to seize him, but he escapes and goes beyond Jordan, where many believe in him.
meaningChecks: Kept Christ as the source’s title without adding a theory of the expected role.

record.title: Peter, Cornelius and the Gentiles
record.summary: Peter has a vision of animals unclean under ritual rules. He is sent to the centurion Cornelius, an army officer. The Spirit falls on the Gentile, or non-Jewish, household, and the Jerusalem church accepts it.

meaning.original: Peter has a vision of unclean animals and is sent to the centurion Cornelius. The Spirit falls on the Gentile household, and the Jerusalem church accepts it.
meaningChecks: Unclean is explained as ritual status, not dirt or illness. Gentile means non-Jewish; the acceptance retains the original “it.”

record.title: Thessalonica, Athens and Corinth
record.summary: Paul preaches in Thessalonica and Berea, speaks to the Areopagus in Athens, and stays in Corinth for eighteen months.

meaning.original: Paul preaches in Thessalonica and Berea, speaks to the Areopagus in Athens, and spends eighteen months in Corinth.
meaningChecks: Kept Areopagus as named in the record; specifying a council, hill or venue would resolve an ambiguity the summary leaves open.
